messages:
Lena Ortiz: Heads-up — QA reported flaky behavior in our React Native WebView sample. Streaming chat sometimes shows chunks arriving out of logical order (e.g. middle of sentence then earlier prefix). Looks like chunk reordering on resume from background.

Ravi Kumar: out of order? HTTP guarantees ordering per TCP stream. Are they using a proxy or service worker?

Lena Ortiz: it's a mobile app WebView. Repro steps: 1) open streaming chat 2) let it stream for a few tokens 3) background the app for ~3-5s 4) foreground -> UI shows fragments shuffled. Happens on Android WebView only (Chromium).

Diego Martins: interesting. My guess: when webview suspends, the renderer may pause JS task runner, and when it resumes, ReadableStream chunks might be delivered in different microtask ordering compared to before. Not true TCP reordering, more like our chunk-assembly relies on per-chunk timing.

Lena Ortiz: i captured a trace: server emitted events A -> B -> C, network trace shows they arrived A B C, but our UI rendered B then A then C. The client-side parser is using delimiter-splitting + push to React state asynchronously which can interleave.

Ravi Kumar: so it's a client ordering bug. Are we using async setState in a loop? If we call setState per chunk without serializing, React might batch updates causing render order differences. Also possible: using Promise.resolve().then() per chunk leads to microtask race.

Diego Martins: Repro patch idea: process chunks on a dedicated microtask queue that preserves arrival order. E.g. push to an internal JS array and only flush to UI on next animationFrame in order. Also ensure parser emits events synchronously in the same tick as chunk arrival to avoid inversion.

Lena Ortiz: another angle: some WebView versions coalesce small chunks when resuming, causing previously emitted chunk boundaries to merge — if our parser assumes one message per chunk we get weird merges. 

Ravi Kumar: SDK parity note: node SDK consumers rarely render incrementally; browser & RN need stronger guarantees. We should document: "do not assume chunk == message" and show a robust client pattern. Add helper: sdk.stream(onEvent) where SDK ensures ordered delivery and reassembly of partial UTF-8 + event delimiting.

Diego Martins: Also saw a case where AbortController.signal.abort() triggered while a chunk decode was in-flight; reader.read() returned done:true but with a trailing partial chunk. Current behavior: SDK emits 'close' and throws away leftover bytes. Propose: on abort, emit 'aborted' with leftover bytes attached so apps can decide (log or try resume).

Lena Ortiz: QA also reported long hang when network toggles (wifi -> cell). Our stream waits ~20s before error. Could we expose a configurable idle timeout per stream (e.g., streamIdleTimeoutMs) so app can surface a better UX?

Ravi Kumar: yes. Default could be 30s idle; SDK should emit `idle_timeout` diagnostic event before force-close, with a reason code. Also ensure we don't auto-retry on partial delivery (see previous threads).

Diego Martins: action items:
- Lena: attach trace + small screen recording to INF-2091 (ETA: today)
- Ravi: add SDK helper `reliableStream(handler, opts)` that does: streaming TextDecoder with {stream:true}, per-event delimiting, ordered internal queue, and abort/idle handling (ETA: this sprint)
- Diego: add small RN sample demonstrating foreground/background repro and a test harness (ETA: next week)

devex-bot: Created ticket INF-2091 "mobile-webview: streaming chunk ordering & abort/idle semantics" and assigned Lena, Ravi, Diego.

Lena Ortiz: thanks. temporary workaround for apps: buffer incoming chunks into an array and only render after a deterministic flush (e.g., requestAnimationFrame) and use TextDecoder stream option. That fixes most shuffles.

Ravi Kumar: will also add a short doc blurb about WebView caveats and recommended patterns in devex/sample-apps/mobile.

Diego Martins: I'll add unit tests simulating microtask reordering + merged chunk boundaries to ensure helper keeps order.

Lena Ortiz: perfect. ping me when the helper lands so QA can re-run.
